# Auralink's patches to MyGo

0001 and 0002 are AudioSmith's patches (AudioSmith @f171c86), carried over unchanged: Auralink shares its UI kit and hits the same MyGo issues; their examples are AudioSmith's, where they were found. 0003 is Auralink's own.

Auralink builds against `third_party/mygo` (the `replace` in `go.mod`): MyGo at the version `go.mod` requires, with these patches, made by `scripts/vendor-mygo.sh` from the module cache. The copy leaves out MyGo's website, docs, examples, CI, tests and test data; `scripts/vendor-mygo.sh --check` tells whether it is exactly what the script makes. Never edit `third_party/mygo` by hand: change a patch and run the script.

Keep each patch small and send it upstream (egoist/mygo); drop it when a release has the fix. With no patch left, delete `third_party/mygo` and the replace (`go mod edit -dropreplace github.com/egoist/mygo`).

| Patch | Why |
|---|---|
| `0001-coretext-own-width.patch` | On macOS a single-line text given exactly its measured width ended in "…" ("M4B（含章节）" in the audiobook's Format control; 177 zh-Hans and 181 English strings of the catalogue at some size), and wrapping text in a box of its own width dropped its last word to a second line. Core Text spaces a bracket apart from a letter of another script; between runs of two fonts it only moves glyphs, so the sum of advances MyGo takes as the width came out short of what `CTTypesetterSuggestLineBreak` needs. Long lines also lost more than Core Text forgives (0.0002 DIPs) to float32 sums. The patch folds run gaps into advances, sums widths in float64 and breaks at width × (1 + 1e-6). The patch header explains it in full. |
| `0002-select-list-scrolls.patch` | `ui.Select`'s list had no height limit and no scroll: a long one (Kokoro's 25 voices, the gallery's categories) ran off the bottom of the window, its last options out of reach. The list now scrolls in the room left below the trigger (at most 20 rows' worth); the highlighted option already scrolled into view. |
| `0003-nonactivating-window.patch` | Auralink's recording pill floats over the app the user dictates into; a click on its buttons must not activate Auralink, or the target app loses its focus and caret and ⌘V pastes elsewhere. `WindowOptions.NonActivating` maps onto the platform's `Focusable` (Windows already gives `WS_EX_NOACTIVATE`); on macOS the window is created as a `MyGoPanel` (NSPanel, `NSWindowStyleMaskNonactivatingPanel` at init, never key or main), and its surface tracks the mouse always (`NSTrackingActiveAlways`), so hover works while another app is active. Changing the class of a live window does not work (M0 spike S3: clicks stopped reaching the app). Such a window cannot take the keyboard: no text inputs. |

Make a patch: copy the module (`go env GOMODCACHE`/github.com/egoist/mygo@VERSION) somewhere writable, `git init` and commit it, change it, run its tests on the Mac and Linux, `git diff > third_party/mygo-patches/000N-name.patch`, then run `scripts/vendor-mygo.sh`.
